newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end up ahead of key events.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end up ahead of key events.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended an abbreviated session firmer on low turnover due to the Good Friday holiday.
Dealers said the release of Japan's industrial production data, showing a 3.4 percent decline in February, failed to move the market as it was in line with expectations.

They said JGB futures rallied in early trade on the back of a short-covering spree in Tokyo but the June contract came up against a large sell order at 125.75. It ended at 125.61 against its opening 125.35.
A dealer with a European house said JGB futures were bought up on talk the Ministry of Finance would conduct an outright bond buying operation, but this failed to materialise.

JGB futures fell on Thursday on reports Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) planned to restructure its operations. Dealers said this was seen as negative for the market as it would alleviate worries about Japan's financial system.
But JGBs were brought off their lows late on Thursday by a senior NCB official's denial of reports that a restructuring plan had been finalised.
"The JGBs fell on news of NCB but I believe they might pick up from here," said the dealer.
A trader with an Asian institution said Friday's gains were exaggerated by a thin market.
December Euroyen ended at its day high of 99.04 against an IMM close at 99.03 on meagre volume of 2,700 lots.

Players are expected to remain cautious in the face of a series of key events next week including the Japanese fiscal year end on Monday and the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey or tankan on Wednesday.
Eurodollar futures were not traded due to the holiday. On Thursday, the September contract finished unchanged against its IMM close at 93.760.
